title: Arterial and venous cocaine plasma concentrations in humans: Relationship to route of administration, cardiovascular effects and subjective effects

claims.statement: In laboratory studies of men who already used cocaine often, smoked and injected cocaine reached the blood within seconds, and the effects they rated peaked within about 1 to 1.5 minutes and had mostly faded within 15 to 30 minutes, while cocaine was still in the blood at 90 minutes; the snorted route was not measured in the studies read. In 9 men on a residential research unit who used both injected and smoked cocaine (study conditions, not amounts to use: 16 or 32 mg injected and 25 or 50 mg smoked, each given over 15 seconds, with each route's doses in rising order about 90 minutes apart), arterial levels peaked about 15 seconds after the dose ended, at roughly ten times the later arm-vein peak (at that moment, after 32 mg injected, 2347 ng/ml in arterial against 27 ng/ml in arm-vein blood), while arm-vein levels peaked at about 4 minutes; the two approached each other within about 20 minutes, and at 90 minutes levels after the higher doses were still above those after the lower ones. Ratings of feeling stimulated, high and liking the drug peaked about 1.0 to 1.5 minutes after either route, stayed raised for about 10 minutes, were low by 15 to 30 minutes and were no longer reported at 90 minutes; blood pressure and heart rate (about 107 beats a minute after the highest doses) peaked within about 1 to 1.5 minutes. Smoked doses gave lower blood levels than injected doses (arm-vein peaks 67 and 143 against 108 and 252 ng/ml), yet peak ratings and peak systolic pressure did not differ significantly between routes in 8 men; because sham smoking itself raised blood pressure and ratings of high, and no effect was compared with placebo or sham, the study cannot show that one route gives a stronger effect for the same blood level. Of 13 men who started, 4 were discharged in the first phase, 3 for transient premature ventricular contractions (extra heartbeats; 2 of them had received only placebo injections) and 1 for chest pain after a single smoked dose, so the men analysed are those who tolerated every dose (Evans et al., 1996). In 4 men given 100 or 200 mg into a vein over 1.5 to 3 minutes after at least 48 hours without cocaine, the highest measured level was in the first arm sample, at 5 minutes, and the level then halved every 40 to 52 minutes after 100 mg and every 79 to 82 minutes after 200 mg; the paper's equations relating half-life to dose rest on five sessions with doses compared mostly between different men, and its early values lie above the assay's calibrated range (Barnett et al., 1981). For snorting, the same paper's figures of about 60% absorbed and an 8-minute absorption half-life come from refitting another laboratory's averaged curves sampled only to 90 minutes, and a 1996 narrative review describes, second-hand from studies not read here, arm-vein peaks about 30 to 40 minutes after snorting against about 5 minutes after injecting or smoking, peak felt effects within 10 to 20 minutes, and effects lasting about 60 minutes or longer after the peak, against about 30 to 45 minutes after injecting or smoking (Hatsukami & Fischman, 1996). None of the studies read tested what happens when people take more because they feel little at first. Both primary studies were small, gave doses in an order that was not randomized and studied only men who used cocaine often. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
claims.magnitude: Evans et al. (1996), 8 to 9 men, 15-second administration: arterial peak about 15 seconds after the end of administration (after 32 mg injected, 2347 ng/ml arterial against 27 ng/ml arm-vein at that moment); arm-vein peaks at about 4 minutes, 108 and 252 ng/ml after 16 and 32 mg injected and 67 and 143 ng/ml after 25 and 50 mg smoked; arterial peaks higher, F(1,7) = 91.353, P < .0001, and earlier, F(1,7) = 52.158, P < .0002, than arm-vein peaks, with no difference in timing by route or dose; injected above smoked peaks, F(1,7) = 7.613, P < .0281. Ratings peaked at about 1.0 (high), 1.25 (liking) and 1.5 minutes (stimulated), stayed raised about 10 minutes, were low by 15 to 30 minutes and absent at 90 minutes (data not shown); heart rate peaked near 107 beats a minute at 1.45 minutes on average; systolic pressure at the first reading, about 1 minute (cuff peaks 158 and 154 mm Hg after 32 mg injected and 50 mg smoked). Barnett et al. (1981), 4 men, 100 or 200 mg into a vein over 1.5 to 3 minutes: 5-minute levels 682 to 1005 ng/ml after 100 mg and 2530 and 3868 ng/ml after 200 mg, the highest measured in each session; terminal half-lives 40.3, 47.2 and 51.5 minutes after 100 mg and 78.9 and 82.3 minutes after 200 mg (51.5 against 82.3 in the one man given both). Snorting, not measured in either study: about 60% absorbed, absorption half-life 8.4 minutes, from a refit of another laboratory's averaged curves (Barnett et al., 1981); arm-vein peak about 30 to 40 minutes, peak felt effects within 10 to 20 minutes, effects lasting about 60 minutes or longer after the peak, as described second-hand by a narrative review (Hatsukami & Fischman, 1996). No interval is given for any time estimate.
